look_here_first: Inspect an opposite leaf pair on an unpruned shoot: blades are thin, usually 1–3 inches long, often hairy beneath along the midvein, with hairy petioles and young stems. Confirm short terminal and upper-axillary white flower panicles.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Evergreen to semi-evergreen, many-stemmed shrub often forming dense thickets by suckering.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, simple, entire, elliptic to oblong, usually 1–3 inches long, thinner than L. lucidum; hairs along underside midvein and on petioles.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Small white four-lobed flowers in shorter terminal or upper-axillary panicles, usually about 2–3 inches long.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Clusters of purple-black to black drupes.

key_traits.label: Stems
key_traits.text: Young twigs often hairy, with lenticels; can form suckering thickets.
